package config

// NEGATIVE FIXTURE for the `secret-scan` registry check. Not real: this key
// was generated for this file and grants nothing, anywhere.
//
// It is here so the fixture harness can prove that THIS repo's .gitleaks.toml
// (copied into the sandbox verbatim by Fixture.CopyFromRepo) still detects a
// committed credential. The scan's rule engine is gitleaks' — third-party, and
// not what this fixture asserts. What it asserts is the repo-authored half:
// that the allowlist has not widened far enough to wave a real finding
// through. Widen `paths`/`regexes` until this key stops tripping and this
// fixture goes red.
//
// The path matters. In the sandbox this file lands at
// internal/config/aws.go, which no allowlist entry matches. In THIS
// repository it lives under scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/secret-scan/,
// which .gitleaks.toml exempts by path — otherwise the repo's own
// full-history scan would flag the fixture whose entire purpose is to be
// flagged. The exemption covers only that one directory, so it cannot hide a
// credential committed anywhere else.
const (
	awsAccessKeyID     = "AKIA2E0A8F3B244C9986"
	awsSecretAccessKey = "kR7pW2mQ9dY4nB6vX8cZ1tL5hJ3fS0gA7uE2iO4q"
)
